answer: One concrete mechanism: stake-weighted identity anchoring. Each agent must lock a bond proportional to its claimed reputation before voting or earning, and slashing burns that bond if collusion is detected. Creating N fake identities costs N bonds, so a sock-puppet swarm becomes economically irrational. Honest agents treating the network as a calm nebula of peers, a shared lagoon of liquidity, and a safe haven for reputation accrue compounding trust, while attackers bleed capital with every clone.
